SUBJECT:  APPROVE THIRD AMENDMENT WITH RICHARDS, WATSON &
  GERSHON FOR LEGAL SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $100,000
  FOR A TOTAL CONTRACT AMOUNT OF $600,000.

ISSUE
Approve the Third Amendment to Legal Services Agreement between the City of
Palmdale and Richards, Watson & Gershon (A-6240) increasing the contract maximum
by $100,000 for a total contract amount of $600,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the Third Amendment to Legal Services Agreement between the City of
  Palmdale and Richards, Watson & Gershon (A-6240) increasing the contract
  maximum by $100,000 for a total contract amount of $600,000.
  2. Authorize the City Manager, or his designee to execute the Third Amendment
  with Richards, Watson & Gershon including making minor and non-substantive
  changes.

BACKGROUND
The law firm of Richards, Watson & Gershon has served the City for over thirty years.
The original contract amount was $250,000 and effective through March 1, 2023.

In May 2020, the City Council approved the First Amendment to the Agreement increasing
the not-to-exceed amount by $100,000.

In September 2020, the City Council approved the Second Amendment increasing the
not-to-exceed agreement amount by $150,000 to $500,000.

  5
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Richards, Watson & Gershon
February 16, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
Richards, Watson & Gershon is currently handling litigation regarding the City’s rent-
control ordinance and various advisory matters. Due to several large litigation matters
and numerous consultations, the Third Amendment to Legal Services Agreement A-6240
will increase the not-to- exceed agreement amount by $100,000 to a total contract amount
of $600,000. This will cover the balance of the litigation, current advisory matters and
any future matters.

FISCAL IMPACT
The Third Amendment to Legal Services Agreement A-6240 will increase the not-to-
exceed agreement amount by $100,000 to $600,000, however, this amount is not
guaranteed. Fees will only be paid to the extent services are provided. Funds for this
agreement are currently budgeted in the City Attorney’s Office budget accounts.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  A. Manage resources, costs and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 1561 AMENDING THE PALMDALE
  MUNICIPAL  CODE  SECTION  2.08.030  REGARDING
  APPOINTMENTS TO BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS BY THE CITY
  COUNCIL

ISSUE
Adopt Ordinance No. 1561 Amending the Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.08.030
regarding appointments to Boards and Commissions by the City Council.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Ordinance No. 1561 Amending the
Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.08.030 regarding appointments to Boards and
Commissions by the City Council.

BACKGROUND
Currently, the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 2.08.030 Mayor to make
appointments reads as follows:

  The Mayor, with the approval of the City Council, shall make all appointments to
  boards, commissions and committees of the City as follows:

  (A) All board and commission vacancies shall be advertised, seeking volunteers
  willing and desiring to be appointed to fill such vacancies. Any person seeking to
  be so appointed must complete and submit the city volunteer application,
  together with any other information requested by the Mayor as appropriate for a
  specific board or commission.

  (B) All such applications shall be provided to the Mayor for review, who shall, at a
  regularly scheduled City Council meeting, nominate, from among such
  applicants, the persons whom the Mayor desires to appoint by making a motion,
  which need not be seconded, for each such appointment.

  24
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Council Appointments
February 16, 2021
Page 2

  (C) If the nomination by the Mayor is approved by a majority vote of the City
  Council, the Mayor may then proceed to appoint the person to the board or
  commission under consideration.

  (D) If the nomination by the Mayor is not approved by a majority vote of the City
  Council, the Mayor will nominate, by motion, a different candidate until someone
  is approved by majority vote of the City Council for the position under
  consideration.

  (E) Persons so appointed shall serve the term of office set by ordinance for such
  board or commission and may only be removed by a majority vote of the City
  Council; provided, however, for those boards or commissions for which residency
  in the City of Palmdale is a requirement, the appointment will automatically
  terminate if the person ceases to be a resident of the City.

  (F) This section is not applicable to appointments to the Planning Commission.
  (Ord. 1505 § 3, 2017; Ord. 1357 § 1, 2008)

DISCUSSION
On January 12, 2021, the City Council directed staff to bring back an amendment to PMC
2.08.030 that would allow each Councilmember to nominate a member to a Board or
Commission. After research and review of multiple cities, it has been determined that the
proposed amendment provides for flexibility while ensuring the process is fair and
equitable. This also meets the desires of the Council which in hopes will reflect adequate
representation of the community.

Proposed Amendment

PMC 2.08.030: Appointments to Boards and Commissions
  Unless otherwise specifically provided in this code or by State Law, the City
  Council shall make all appointments to boards, commissions and committees of
  the City as follows:

  (A) All board and commission vacancies shall be advertised, seeking volunteers
  willing and desiring to be appointed to fill such vacancies. Any person seeking to
  be so appointed must complete and submit the city volunteer application,
  together with any other information requested by the City Council as appropriate
  for a specific board or commission.

  (B) All such applications shall be provided to the City Council for review, who
  shall, at a regularly scheduled City Council meeting, nominate, from among such
  applicants, the persons whom a City Councilmember desires to appoint by
  making a motion which need not be seconded, for each such appointment.

  25

Re: Council Appointments

  (C) If the nomination by the City Councilmember is approved by a majority vote
  of the City Council, the City Council may then proceed to appoint the person to
  the board or commission under consideration.

  (D) If the nomination by the City Council is not approved by a majority vote of the
  City Council, the City Council will nominate, by motion, a different candidate until
  someone is approved by majority vote of the City Council for the position under
  consideration.

  (E) All members of boards, commissions and committees serve at the pleasure
  of the City Council and are subject to removal by a majority vote of the City
  Council.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.

 FROM:  CITY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE

 SUBJECT:  INFORMATION ITEM: REVIEW AND RECEIVE REPORT ON THE
  FUNCTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY AS THE CITY PROSECUTOR

ISSUE
Receive information regarding prosecutorial services of the City Attorney’s office and the
legal authority for the City Attorney to prosecute state law misdemeanors committed
within the City.

RECOMMENDATION
Receive information and provide direction to staff.

BACKGROUND
At the City Council meeting on February 2, 2021, the council directed staff to return with
a report on the legal authority for the City Attorney to prosecute state law misdemeanors
committed within the City. This report will address the inquiry.

Generally, the office of the District Attorney of the respective county within which a city
resides is responsible for the prosecution of all state law misdemeanors committed within
the jurisdiction. (Gov. Code § 26500).

At present, the City Attorney’s office has significant prosecutorial authority to prosecute
violations of the Palmdale Municipal Code and Ordinances. Palmdale Municipal Code
section 2.06.060 provides this authority; “(Powers and Duties) provides the following:
“The City Attorney shall have the following powers and duties…(b) to initiate all
proceedings in law or equity for the criminal or civil enforcement of all City ordinances
and for the defense of the City in all legal actions.” These violations can be charged, or
filed, as administrative actions, infractions, or misdemeanors. The associated penalty for
such is graduated accordingly. California State Law (Civ. Code. §731) authorizes the City
Attorney’s office to prosecute public nuisance actions in the name of the People of the
State of California.

  30
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: City Prosecutions
February 16, 2021
Page 2

Presented herein is the legal authority for the City Council to expand the role of the City
Attorney’s office to prosecute all or some state law misdemeanors committed within our
jurisdiction.

DISCUSSION
The prosecution of state misdemeanor offenses is assigned generally to the District
Attorney of each county. However, under California law City Attorneys may also be
authorized to prosecute such offenses within their respective cities by either 1) District
Attorney consent or 2) express charter language.

  A. District Attorney Consent

Government Code section 41803.5, applicable to both general law and charter cities,
provides:

  With the consent of the District Attorney of the county, the City
  Attorney of any general law city or chartered city within the
  county may prosecute any misdemeanor committed within the
  city arising out of a violation of state law…

Under this section the District Attorney can simply provide consent to the City Attorney to
prosecute state law misdemeanors committed within the City of Palmdale. This requires
little more than City Council direction and District Attorney consent. Items of concern are
whether the political and policy interests of the District Attorney support the decision of
transferring his existing authority over state law misdemeanor prosecutions to the City
Attorney. That issue, as well as whether the City should devote resources to fund a
misdemeanor prosecution unit in the Office of the City Attorney, is outside the scope of
this report.

Several cities in California have requested and received consent from their District
Attorney to prosecute state law misdemeanors, including but not limited to: San
Bernardino, Los Angeles, Burbank, Anaheim, Long Beach, Pasadena, San Diego,
Huntington Beach, Santa Barbara and Santa Monica. Each of the above cities has a
prosecution division/City Prosecutor in the City Attorney’s Office.

Other cities, like Oakland have opted, with the concurrence of the District Attorney, to
only prosecute “quality of life” or lower-level state law misdemeanors, with the District
Attorney prosecuting more serious misdemeanors.

  B. Charter Amendment

If the District Attorney refuses to provide consent, state law provides charter cities with
an alternative.

  31
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: City Prosecutions
February 16, 2021
Page 3

Government Code section 72193, applicable only to charter cities, states:

  Whenever the charter of any city…creates the office of the city
  prosecutor…and charges such prosecutor with the duty, when
  authorized by law, of prosecuting misdemeanor offenses
  arising out of violations of state laws…(a) [t]he city prosecutor
  shall prosecute all such misdemeanors committed within the
  city, and handle all appeals arising from it…

When the provisions of section 72193 are implemented by a charter city, the City Attorney
has the primary duty of prosecuting state misdemeanors within the city, with the district
attorney acting in a subsidiary or “backup” role. (See Menveg v. Municipal Court (1964)
226 Cal.App.2d 569, 571-572. This “backup” role may be viewed as analogous to the role
of the Attorney General in cases where for some reason a District Attorney is unable to
prosecute and offense or where there has been a breakdown in the law within the county.
(See 79 Ops.Cal.Atty.Gen. 221, 223 (Cal. AG 1996)

Accordingly, the City Council may submit an amendment to the voters asking them to
amend the City Charter (Palmdale’s is silent in that regard) to require the City Attorney to
prosecute state law misdemeanors and, thereby, recovering the prosecutorial duties
assigned to the District Attorney.

This is a common approach. As recently as November 2, 2020, the City of Alameda in
association with the general election, amended their charter to reflect the above.

The unknown anomaly, however, is that of the cities listed above, they have all
established strict control over law enforcement; they have not just a City Prosecutions
Division, but also their own police department. Further research is necessary to determine
feasibility under our present agreement with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department.

FISCAL IMPACT
The fiscal impact of creating a City Prosecutions division will be fully vetted if directed by
the City Council. In the interim, looking at other City Prosecution Divisions, we can
estimate the costs associated with the task.

Below is a table of a sample of Southern California cities that have a City Prosecutions
division, and the attorney personnel staffed therein:

office. This includes victim’s services, investigators, and witness coordination. The
